identity: Concept of the keeper, the player character of a co-op game about guarding a giant dragon egg on a stormy mountain at night. Exactly one keeper, full body, standing in a neutral relaxed pose in front three-quarter view, holding a lit hand lantern in the left hand and a tall wooden spear upright in the right hand, the spear butt resting on the ground. Hooded cloak over a padded tunic, a belt with one small pouch, sturdy boots. Brave and friendly, face visible under the hood. No other characters, no creature, no egg, no extra props, no text.

Key art at the gameplay camera for a co-op game about guarding a giant dragon egg. Image 1 is this game's keeper: the three keepers in this scene wear exactly that outfit and keep its body proportions, lantern and spear; do not copy its grey background or its pose. Night on a flat rocky ledge high on a stormy mountain, above a sea of clouds. In the middle of the frame: a giant dragon egg, about three times as tall as a keeper, standing upright in a round nest of stones and branches. The egg's shell is smooth and whole; it glows from inside and is the brightest thing in the image; only exactly 3 thin glowing cracks run down from its top. Exactly 6 torches on poles stand evenly spaced in a circle around the nest: 2 in front, 1 on each side, 2 behind. Exactly 3 small keepers stand on the ledge around the egg, guarding it with spears ready and lanterns raised: one at the front left, one at the front right, one behind the egg on the right, all facing outward toward the dark. Beyond the torch ring the ledge drops away into dark storm clouds; exactly 2 sky thieves glide as dark winged silhouettes near the top edge of the frame, far from the egg, edged by a distant lightning flash. The thieves are masked raiders hanging under wide, ragged, bat-like glider wings; they are not dragons and not birds: no long neck, no tail. The egg is the focal point; the keepers are small but clearly readable; the thieves are the threat. No dragon anywhere, no text, no user interface.
